pharm: A 5-nitroimidazole (metronidazole family) that acts as an electron-affinic hypoxic-cell radiosensitizer in head and neck cancer radiotherapy and as an antiprotozoal. Reduced nitro intermediates damage microbial DNA, and in hypoxic tumor cells it mimics oxygen to enhance radiation-induced DNA damage. Not FDA-approved (brand Naxogin).
quick: Radiosensitizer (DAHANCA): 1.2 g/m2 orally ~1.5 h before each radiotherapy fraction; antiprotozoal: oral per indication
May take with food; for trichomoniasis often taken with a main meal
No detailed adjustment; caution in significant impairment
No detailed adjustment; caution in significant impairment
Nausea/vomiting and compliance; neurologic status on prolonged/high-dose use
summary: Nimorazole is a 5-nitroimidazole, in the same chemical family as metronidazole, with two distinct roles: as an electron-affinic hypoxic-cell radiosensitizer added to curative radiotherapy for head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (the standard of care in Denmark via the DAHANCA protocol), and as an antiprotozoal for trichomoniasis, amoebiasis, and giardiasis. As a radiosensitizer it mimics oxygen in radioresistant hypoxic tumor cells, fixing radiation-induced DNA damage so those cells become as radiosensitive as oxygenated ones; the DAHANCA radiosensitizer dose is 1.2 g/m2 orally about 90 minutes before each radiotherapy fraction. As an antimicrobial, its reduced nitro group damages microbial/protozoal DNA. A key advantage over metronidazole/misonidazole is effective radiosensitization without dose-limiting neurotoxicity; nausea and vomiting are the dominant adverse effects. Like other nitroimidazoles it can cause a disulfiram-like reaction with alcohol. It is NOT FDA-approved (EMA orphan designation 2011). NOTE: This record draws on the DAHANCA guideline, published trials, and class references.
indications: Hypoxic-cell radiosensitizer added to curative radiotherapy for head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (standard of care in Denmark - DAHANCA protocol)

dosage.t: About 90 minutes (1.5 h) before each radiotherapy fraction, 5 days/week
dosage.n: Given with each daily fraction over the radiotherapy course

dosage.d: 2 g as a single dose (with a main meal), or 1 g every 12 h x3 doses, or 250 mg twice daily x6 days
dosage.n: Treat the sexual partner; may repeat after 1 month

dosage.d: 500 mg-1 g every 12 hours (or 500 mg twice daily x5-7 days)

admin: Give the radiosensitizer dose about 1.5 hours before the radiotherapy fraction so tumor levels peak at irradiation
May be given by feeding tube in head and neck cancer patients unable to swallow
Antiemetic premedication is commonly used to manage nausea/vomiting during radiotherapy
Take antiprotozoal doses orally; trichomoniasis single dose is often taken with a main meal
Avoid alcohol during and shortly after treatment (disulfiram-like reaction)
moa: Nimorazole is a 5-nitroimidazole. As an antimicrobial/antiprotozoal, its nitro group is reduced intracellularly in anaerobic and protozoal organisms to reactive intermediates that damage DNA and inhibit nucleic acid synthesis, killing organisms such as Trichomonas vaginalis, Entamoeba histolytica, and Giardia lamblia. As a radiosensitizer, its high electron affinity lets it mimic oxygen in hypoxic tumor cells: in the absence of oxygen it is reduced to species that 'fix' radiation-induced free-radical DNA damage, rendering radioresistant hypoxic cells as radiosensitive as oxygenated cells and thereby enhancing radiation-induced cell kill.

absolute: Known hypersensitivity to nimorazole or other nitroimidazoles
relative: Active CNS or neurologic disease (class caution)
monitor: Neurologic status on prolonged or high cumulative dosing
Tumor response in the oncology setting

preg: As with the nitroimidazole class, nimorazole is generally avoided in pregnancy, especially the first trimester, and should be used only if clearly necessary.
lact: Caution is advised during breastfeeding, consistent with the nitroimidazole class.
renal: No detailed dose-adjustment scheme is available; pharmacokinetics are largely linear with rapid absorption and a short half-life. Use caution in significant renal impairment.
hepatic: No detailed dose-adjustment scheme is available. Use caution in significant hepatic impairment.

major: Alcohol - disulfiram-like reaction (nausea, vomiting, flushing, headache), a class effect of nitroimidazoles
moderate: Other drugs metabolized similarly to nitroimidazoles (class-level caution)
minor: Class effects on warfarin/anticoagulant response are described for nitroimidazoles - monitor if co-administered
interactions.food: May be taken with food; the trichomoniasis single dose is often taken with a main meal.
interactions.alcohol: Avoid alcohol during and shortly after treatment because of a disulfiram-like reaction (note: reported to be less pronounced with nimorazole than with tinidazole, but avoidance is still advised).

serious: Rare severe CNS events at very high doses (seizures, encephalopathy, coma)
rare: Peripheral neuropathy on prolonged use (notably less than with metronidazole)
emergency: Seizures / encephalopathy at very high doses

monitoring: Nausea/vomiting and antiemetic response during the radiotherapy course
Treatment compliance with the radiosensitizer schedule
Neurologic status on prolonged or high cumulative dosing
Tumor response in the oncology setting
counsel: Do NOT drink alcohol while taking this medicine or for a short time afterward - it can cause flushing, nausea, and vomiting
If used with radiotherapy, take each dose about 1.5 hours before your radiation session, on schedule
Nausea and vomiting are common - your team may give you anti-sickness medicine to help
Report numbness or tingling in your hands or feet if you are on a long course
Take the full course as prescribed
pk: Rapidly absorbed orally; radiosensitizer dose timed ~1.5 h before irradiation
Linear relationship between peak plasma concentration and dose; good tumor penetration (tumor/plasma ~0.8-1.3)
Short half-life; radiosensitizer dosed before each fraction
Store at room temperature, protected from light and moisture
pearls: The prototypical clinically used NITROIMIDAZOLE hypoxic radiosensitizer - cornerstone of the DAHANCA protocol in Denmark for head and neck cancer
Mimics oxygen in hypoxic tumor cells, fixing radiation-induced DNA damage to overcome hypoxia-related radioresistance
DAHANCA 5 trial: adding nimorazole to radiotherapy improved 5-year locoregional control (49% vs 33%) and disease-specific survival
Key advantage over metronidazole/misonidazole: effective radiosensitization WITHOUT dose-limiting neurotoxicity
Disulfiram-like reaction with alcohol (class effect) - counsel to avoid alcohol
NOT FDA-approved (EMA orphan designation 2011); also used as an antiprotozoal (trichomoniasis, amoebiasis, giardiasis)
missed: For the antiprotozoal indication, take a missed dose when remembered unless it is almost time for the next dose; do not double up. For the radiosensitizer schedule, follow the radiotherapy protocol guidance if a dose or fraction is missed and do not double subsequent doses.
overdose: Overdose is dominated by gastrointestinal effects and, at extreme doses, central nervous system toxicity (seizures, encephalopathy). There is no specific antidote; management is supportive with seizure precautions and monitoring.
